title: introducing kiosk
excerpt: A little project I spent some of my time with.
content.markdown:
I finished a new version of a project I called [kiosk](https://kiosk-vbalaguera.vercel.app/kiosk "https://kiosk-vbalaguera.vercel.app/kiosk"). A simple news API app. At this moment, uses The New York Times API only as a source of external content.

Implemented functions such as:

-   auth (using Firebase).

-   multiple news sections.

-   news search.

-   sharing options through email, telegram, copying the link to the clipboard, and other venues.

-   CRUD capabilities using Firebase:

    -   save any news articles in your favorites.
    -   filter favorites by sections.
    -   users can create notes on their dashboard page.

-   daily backups of all main news sections by using python (in case the API has reached its maximum number of daily calls, searching will only display a random news section)

More to come. Enjoy.

title: current developments
excerpt: Minor new features and trinkets. Implemented for fun.
content.markdown:
When I created [this blog](https://blackguard.es "https://blackguard.es"), I followed a basic white text/black background color scheme. Typical but functional. I decided to change it into new ones that you can see right now. The dark mode uses Prussian Blue/Berlin Blue/Turnbull’s blue, a color I always liked since I discovered cyanotypes back in the early 2000s. The sepia comes from one of the pens that I daily use.

Here's a cyanotype example:



![ephoto5m.jpeg](https://media.graphassets.com/Xk9ICu5cTCqVQrPFMV7Q "ephoto5m.jpeg")

[Source](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:John_Frederick_William_Herschel_-_Lady_with_a_harp_1842.jpg "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:John_Frederick_William_Herschel\_-\_Lady_with_a_harp_1842.jpg").

The second feature is a small music player in [this much I know](https://www.blackguard.es/this-much-I-know "https://www.blackguard.es/this-much-I-know"). I originally recreated one using plain vanilla js, but I wanted to see how to create a React one. At the moment it has some serious limitations: there's no auto skip when the song that's playing ends, and if you try to use the player between pages (by setting it anywhere in the current layouts), it will reload every time.



Problems to research and fix. It's fun.

title: My favorite obsession
excerpt: About coding Tetris, for learning and academic purposes.
content.markdown:
Have you ever had any unexpected, quirky habit that you eventually transformed into another ritual?

I do not know why, but since it is one of my favorite games of all time, I always ended up checking out how to code Tetris when starting to learn a new language.

It started by [coding it in Javascript](https://github.com/VBalaguera/tetris-upgrade "https://github.com/VBalaguera/tetris-upgrade") (original tutorial by [Ania Kubow](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC5DNytAJ6_FISueUfzZCVsw "https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC5DNytAJ6_FISueUfzZCVsw") [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAUn1Lom6dw&ab_channel=freeCodeCamp.org "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAUn1Lom6dw&ab_channel=freeCodeCamp.org")). Tutorials are great starting points for any developer and/or aficionado, but the real beauty is to leave behind the good ol' _monkey see, monkey do_ scenario. [By thoroughly reading and understanding any code, and subsequently testing and implementing new features.](https://upbeat-newton-d93296.netlify.app/ "https://upbeat-newton-d93296.netlify.app/")

A few days ago I finished a Python one. So far it's [only on its repo](https://github.com/VBalaguera/tetris-python/ "https://github.com/VBalaguera/tetris-python/"). Need more functions, more beauty. [pygame](https://www.pygame.org/ "https://www.pygame.org/") is fun so far.

Question is, which language will be the next one?

title: Not the games, not the games, not the games
content.markdown:
So, I have started studying Python over the past month. I am more than interested in expanding what I supposedly know and submerge myself into the outlands of backend development, or something. When you start a task like this one, it always feels like probing the unknown.

To say that Python has been hugely entertaining so far would be an understatement. The nuts, bolts and logic of any language are substantially more interesting than their potential applications because that is the frontier. A frontier I will only witness from the stands, but still.

So far I've only been coding small e-commerce related apps and games. So many games. I need to deep down on Django and take a look at how to put everything, and more, out there.

Need to keep studying and working. This is fun.

In the meantime, this is where I get off.

title: A bug that got my attention
excerpt: When git just refused to work.
content.markdown:
Have you ever encountered a bug so strange, so out of nowhere, so baffling that you just can't find many resources to fix it, if any?

I am currently using Git 2.35.1 through Big Sur (updating to Monterrey at the moment), and for the past few weeks, a weird bug kept popping up and becoming more and more common. Any files named index.js would get automatically ignored and .gitignore would be rendered useless. But why?

I started noticing it when running npx create-next-app or create-react-app. Seemingly, this bug would randomly disappear for a while. Last week it came back with a vengeance. It would not away. Was it an error within node or npm? Nah. Every time I run git init, all that madness would come back. Now, maybe git needed an update through homebrew? Nope. What about a full installation? Doable, but as far as I know any newer git versions just update 2.30.1 Apple Git-130 and that's integrated into the OS, hard.

So, I started waving my arms and asking for help until someone asked me if I had a _global_ .gitignore in my /users/ folder. And bingo: there it was. Sometime in the past, I added index.js to that file. Somehow I was using that file only on projects and not all of them. After erasing it, Git was working as before. I updated it back to 2.35.1, got the same results.

What a headache, but an entertaining one if I have to be honest.
